Type \(\le\) as <= and \(\ge\) as >=, for example 4x+9y<=72. Use the letters x and y as defined in the question.

generalfeedback.text:
For each line, find its equation from two points on it, then test a point of R such as \({@rp@}\) to choose the sign. A solid line gives \(\le\) or \(\ge\); a dashed line gives \(\lt\) or \(\gt\).

\(L_1\): \({@td[1]@}\). \(L_2\): \({@td[2]@}\). \(L_3\): \({@td[3]@}\).

The shaded side of each line is the part we do not want, so R is on the other side.

questiondescription.text:
Linear Programming: inequalities from a graph

Grade 12 CBE Core 1.4 (b) / Essential 1.4 (b): Read three boundary lines of a region, with the unwanted sides shaded and each line solid or dashed, and write the inequality each line gives.

Core and Essential

This question is adapted from Chapter 1, Section D, questions 6 and 7 of Ling, J., Scruton, P., Shilton, S. and West, H., SMP GCSE Mathematics: Higher 2 for AQA, Edexcel and OCR two-tier GCSE mathematics, Cambridge University Press, 2007: writing the inequalities that define a region, changed to a region left clear with the unwanted sides shaded and solid or dashed boundaries, with new regions.
